blogs.title: When Does a Computer 'Receive' a Notice? 5th Circuit Modernizes Louisiana Insurance Statute
blogs.description: This post analyzes the Fifth Circuit's interpretation of the term 'receipt' under Louisiana insurance cancellation statutes. The court held that an automated email received by an insurer's computer system satisfies the statutory requirement for receipt, even if human possession occurs later. We examine the implications of applying legacy statutory language to modern web services and automated cancellation systems, discussing whether this approach balances consumer protection with technological efficiency.

blogs.title: Strict Adherence or Strict Textualism? The 5th Circuit on Signature Requirements in Louisiana Insurance Law
blogs.description: Louisiana law mandates 'strict adherence' to insurance cancellation procedures to protect consumers, yet the Fifth Circuit ruled that a signature is not required on the cancellation certification. This post explores the tension between the state's protective doctrine and the federal court's textualist refusal to read additional requirements into the statute. We discuss whether this ruling dilutes the consumer safeguards intended by the 'strict adherence' standard.

blogs.title: Federal Courts and State Law: Why the 5th Circuit Declined Certification in Williams v. GoAuto
blogs.description: Plaintiffs requested that the Fifth Circuit certify questions of Louisiana statutory interpretation to the Louisiana Supreme Court. The court declined, citing the 'compelling reason' standard from Jefferson v. Lead Indus. Ass'n. This post examines the procedural dynamics of federal courts interpreting state law without certification, analyzing when the Fifth Circuit chooses to decide state law itself versus deferring to the state's highest court.
